title: Why Five? — The Grand Equivalence
description: The four faces of five — arithmetic, spectral, Galois, trigonometric — shown to be one theorem, plus the divisibility law across all cycles. Every claim binds to a machine-checked theorem in the Brockian verified core; unbacked claims render BLOCKED. A picture cannot outrun its proof.

claims.claim: For a prime p, these are equivalent: p=5; φ−1 is a C_p eigenvalue; ℚ(2cos 2π/p) is quadratic; 2cos(2π/p)=φ−1.
φ − 1 is an adjacency eigenvalue of the cycle Cₙ if and only if 5 divides n.
The prime uniqueness theorem is recovered as a corollary: φ−1 ∈ spec(C_p) ⟺ p=5.
The pentagon's fundamental mode equals the golden value: 2·cos(2π/5) = φ − 1.
[ℚ(2cos 2π/p):ℚ] = (p−1)/2 for every odd prime p — the general Galois degree.
Every circulant mode 2·cos(2πk/n) is an adjacency eigenvalue of Cₙ.
